title: Absorbing polynomial factors
statement: Let $\lambda,I,\varepsilon$ be real numbers with $0<\lambda\le 1/2$, $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, and $\varepsilon\le I$. For every natural number $k$ satisfying $k\le 3I/\varepsilon$, we have $\frac{4I^3}{\varepsilon^2}\left(\frac{9}{\lambda}\right)^k\le\left(\frac{1}{\lambda}\right)^{100I/\varepsilon}$.
replaced: Let $0<\lambda\le1/2$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\varepsilon\le I$, and $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le3I/\varepsilon$. Then $(4I^3/\varepsilon^2)(9/\lambda)^k\le(1/\lambda)^{100I/\varepsilon}$.
